allowed_claim: Use the current evidence to choose benchmark semantics: held-key delay and trace-on per-key Playwright actions are automation stressors, not human typing models.
current_evidence: Raw CDP held-key reproduces the slow band; trace-on per-key Playwright actions insert snapshot work; complete-keypress/tap rows are a different metric family.
blocked_overclaim: Claiming trace-on per-key Playwright actions are more realistic because they are faster.
required_next_evidence: One exact CI-helper compatibility check if the helper spelling changes; otherwise no more broad JS delay rows.

allowed_claim: Say elapsed post-keyup waiting, raw CDP packet shape, and DOM key-event payload do not explain the fast path in the current evidence.
current_evidence: Corrected raw-CDP packets and matched DOM signatures stay slow; ordinary waits through about 5008ms stay in the 21-24ms keypress band.
blocked_overclaim: Explaining runtime-repeat or trace-on fast rows as the browser merely having more time to rest.
required_next_evidence: None unless a new browser build changes the ordinary-wait controls.

allowed_claim: Say repeated direct Runtime.evaluate or Runtime.callFunctionOn checkpoints change the measured Gutenberg input slice.
current_evidence: Direct runtime repeats move raw CDP from about 21.5ms to about 15-16ms at x7 and about 13ms at x17.
blocked_overclaim: Naming V8, microtasks, scheduler priority, or OS state from p50 dose response alone.
required_next_evidence: Trace-off protocol sidecar first; then per-retained-key scheduler/V8 trace that tracks x0/x1/x3/x7/x11/x17.

allowed_claim: Say default trace-on Playwright per-key calls are a measurement perturbation and explain the full low-latency band in those rows.
current_evidence: Trace-on per-key keyboard.press and trace-on raw CDP plus page.evaluate hit about 11.3ms; trace-off versions are much slower, and protocol logs show captureSnapshot between keys.
blocked_overclaim: Using Playwright tracing as both the perturbation and the only observer, or treating snapshot-inserted work as user typing.
required_next_evidence: Separate low-overhead protocol log and trace-on/off observer controls that isolate captureSnapshot or related snapshot commands.

allowed_claim: Leave the exact Chromium state unnamed for now.
current_evidence: Current artifacts identify wait/checkpoint contrasts but do not include scheduler queues, V8 execution, microtask checkpoints, input priority, or aligned OS counters.
blocked_overclaim: Calling the mechanism V8, microtasks, scheduler, input priority, cache, or power state without a recorded per-key state variable.
required_next_evidence: Protocol sidecar plus runtime scheduler/V8 trace that predicts fast and slow retained samples across wait/checkpoint, dose-response, and snapshot rows.

allowed_claim: Treat V8/microtask as an open candidate, not a conclusion.
current_evidence: Runtime commands are sufficient to move the path, but current traces do not expose V8 execution or microtask slices in the key window.
blocked_overclaim: Inferring V8 or microtask state from command count alone.
required_next_evidence: V8 execution and microtask checkpoint events aligned to previous keyup, runtime commands, next keydown, and EventDispatch.

allowed_claim: Treat scheduler/input-priority as an open candidate, not a conclusion.
current_evidence: Runtime checkpoint and CPU/QoS controls both imply state below Gutenberg selectors, but current trace categories are render/screenshot oriented.
blocked_overclaim: Explaining the split as queueing or priority without task queue, priority, thread, or EventDispatch alignment.
required_next_evidence: Chromium task queue, scheduler priority, input task state, process/thread ids, and main-thread task boundaries per retained key.

allowed_claim: Treat OS power/QoS/cache as a lower-layer candidate that can explain or confound the runtime trace result.
current_evidence: Separate CPU/QoS controls move the same Gutenberg path between latency bands, but runtime-repeat rows are not joined to OS counters.
blocked_overclaim: Calling the checkpoint mechanism purely Chromium-internal before matching frequency, residency, QoS, scheduler, and cache state.
required_next_evidence: Optional OS-counter join with renderer pid/thread, powermetrics or trace sample ids, frequency/residency/QoS, and source spans.

allowed_claim: Say the browser checkpoint is real but Gutenberg source fanout supplies the multi-millisecond scale.
current_evidence: Native contenteditable moves only about 0.3-0.4ms under the same runtime-repeat grid; Gutenberg large-post rows move by several milliseconds.
blocked_overclaim: Claiming the browser checkpoint alone explains product-scale latency.
required_next_evidence: Matched browser trace plus Gutenberg source spans and native listener spans on the same runtime rows.

allowed_claim: Keep user/plugin product-latency ranking separate from the benchmark-artifact mechanism.
current_evidence: Current rows use a vanilla large-post fixed-x insertion stressor; workload audits show correction, selection, paste, IME, media/pattern, long-session, and plugin-heavy strata are missing.
blocked_overclaim: Using the runtime checkpoint artifact to rank real editing workloads or plugin-heavy sessions.
required_next_evidence: Recorded or synthetic workload replay with behavior assertions, visual/source endpoints, and per-stratum owner rankings.
